items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7445

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the banking law and the general business law, in
relation to reporting by banking organizations, conforming criminal
provisions of the mortgage banking article to those in the mortgage
loan originator article, permitting remote deposit capture machines,
clarifying the definition of capital impairment for banking
institutions, reducing operating expenses of the banking department
and making other technical changes


 PURPOSE :

This bill would make various technical and clarifying amendments to
the Banking Law ("BL") and the General Business Law ("GBL") to reduce
the operating costs of the Banking Department ("Department"),
facilitate operation, of banks chartered under New York law and make
various technical changes to the Banking Law.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would amend BL § 2 to provide a definition of
the term Superintendent.

Section 2 of the bill would amend BL § 2 to provide a definition of
the term remote deposit capture machine, a machine located at a
business customer's place of business and operated by the customer's
employees, that remotely transmits check data to a bank.

Section 3 of the bill would amend BL § 28-b(3)(a) to clarify the ATMs
to which the section applies.

Section 4 of the bill would amend BL § 37 with regard to the
Superintendent's ability to require the filing of periodic reports of
condition from banking institutions.

Section 5 of the bill would amend BL § 39 to clarify the grounds for
the Superintendent's issuance of a regulatory enforcement order based
on a deficiency in an institution's capital condition.

Section 6 of the bill would amend BL § 42 with regard to the posting
of information concerning the work of the Department. The amendment
would give the Superintendent the flexibility to post notices more
than once a week.

Section 7 of the bill would delete Subdivision 2 of BL § 75-g, which
requires the Department to provide a report to the Legislature with
respect to compliance by banks with the ATM Safety Act.

Sections 8 through 10 of the bill would amend BL §§ 105-a, 240-a and
396-a, respectively, to include remote deposit capture machines within
the ambit of these sections.

Section 11 of the bill would amend the heading of Article 12-D to
clarify that the article covers mortgage brokers and mortgage loan
servicers in addition to mortgage bankers.

Section 12 of the bill would amend paragraph (c) of subdivision 2 of
BL § 590 to clarify the provision by insertion of a comma.

Section 13 of the bill would amend BL § 592 to conform the felony
restrictions imposed on mortgage bankers to those imposed on mortgage
loan originators. The Banking Department would be permanently
prohibited from licensing a felon guilty of a fraud related crime.
There would be a seven-year bar on licensing for those convicted of
all other felonies. As with the felony restrictions applicable to
mortgage loan originators, these amended restrictions would bar the
Department from licensing a mortgage banker if an individual
associated with such entity has one of the listed felony convictions,
notwithstanding any other provision of New York law.

Section 14 of the bill would amend BL § 592-a to conform the felony
restrictions on mortgage brokers to those imposed on mortgage loan
originators and mortgage bankers.

Section 15 of the bill would amend BL § 601-a with regard to branches
and agencies of foreign banking corporations. It would treat a branch
or agency of a foreign banking corporation licensed under BL Article V
as a banking institution for the purposes of the Section.

Section 16 of the bill would amend BL § 604-a to treat a branch or
agency of a foreign banking corporation as a banking institution with
regard to the transfer of fiduciary relationships.

Section 17 of the bill would amend BL § 606 to clarify the grounds for
the Superintendent to take possession of a banking institution based
on the institution's capital level.  The provision is amended to
reference modem capital standards; in particular, federal banking
agency capital standards.

Section 18 of the bill would amend BL § 609 to eliminate references to
industrial banks, and to make the section gender neutral.

Section 19 of the bill would amend GBL § 520-c to allow the Banking
Department to make available information on credit cards more
cost-effectively than is required by current law.  GBL § 520-c
requires the Superintendent to conduct an annual survey of information
with respect to credit cards, such as annual percentage rates, annual
fees, per-transaction charges, late payment fees and grace period, and
to make such information available to members of the public. This
survey has proved very expensive to conduct and collate, and is
wasteful, given the availability of similar information on a number of
financial websites. The bill would eliminate the need to conduct the
survey and would instead direct the Department to make such
information available on a toll-free telephone line and on its
internet website (either directly or through hyperlinks to other
sites).

Section 20 of the bill would provide for the effective date of the
bill. All provisions would be effective upon enactment, except for the
requirement of credit card issuers to print certain information on
credit card statements, which would become effective 30 days after the
bill becomes law.

 EXISTING LAW :

BL § 28-b(3) provides standards for evaluating the Community
Reinvestment Act practices of banking institutions.

BL § 37 contains the procedures to be followed by the Superintendent
when requesting institutions to submit quarterly reports of condition.

BL § 39 sets the various circumstances under which the Superintendent
can impose orders on regulated entities. Currently, the language used
in Section 39 concerning imposing an order for deficient capital
levels contains only a reference to "making good an impairment of
capital", which is an outdated concept as it relates to capital
adequacy. This is particularly true for banking institutions, which
currently have very detailed capital ratio requirements established
under federal law and regulations.
BL § 42 requires the Superintendent to publish a weekly bulletin
regarding the Department's activities.

BL § 75-g requires the Department to provide a report to the
Legislature with respect to compliance by banks with the ATM Safety
Act.

BL §§ 105-a and 240-a set forth the authority of banks, trust
companies and savings banks to operate electronic facilities.

BL § 396-a sets forth the authority of savings and loan associations
to operate electronic facilities.

Article 12-D of the BL provides for the regulation of mortgage
bankers, mortgage brokers and mortgage loan servicers. The current
title of the article does not reflect the extent of its reach.

BL § 590(2)(c) authorizes licensees and registrants under Article 12-D
to apply for branch offices.

BL § 592(2) sets forth the restrictions on felons who apply for
licenses as mortgage bankers or who work for such entities. The
amendments would conform these standards to those applicable to
mortgage loan originators.

BL § 592-a(2) sets forth the restrictions on felons who apply for
registration as mortgage brokers or who work for such entities. The
amendments would conform these standards to those applicable to
mortgage loan originators.

BL § 601-a provides the circumstances pursuant to which various types
of banking institutions can enter into purchase and assumption
agreements.

BL § 604-a allows various banking institutions to transfer their
fiduciary relationships.

BL § 606(1)(e) contains one ground, relating to erosion of an
institution's capital level, on which the Superintendent may take
possession of a banking organization. The current language in this
section is inadequate to reflect modem capital concepts and when a
banking organization is considered to have deficient regulatory
capital.

BL § 609 sets forth the circumstances where the Superintendent may
allow certain banking institutions to resume business after he or she
has taken possession of them.

BL § 599-b provides the definitions used in the regulation of mortgage
loan originators.

GBL § 520-c requires the Superintendent to conduct an annual survey of
information with respect to credit cards, such as annual percentage
rates, annual fees, per-transaction charges, late payment fees and
grace period, and to make such information available to members of the
public.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new bill.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :

This bill continues the Banking Department's longstanding effort to
update its statutory framework for the regulation of entities subject
to its jurisdiction.
Many of the amendments in the bill are non-substantive and would not
change the way the Banking Law is currently interpreted. The
amendments in sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 11, 12, and 19 are designed to
clarify existing law or interpretations.

The amendment in Section 5 of the bill is intended to provide a more
accurate description of the capital deficiency scenarios in which the
Superintendent will impose a regulatory order.

The amendment in Section 6 would allow the Department to post items in
its "bulletin" on days other the regular Friday printing. This will
make some items available for a longer period than would otherwise be
possible if items are posted only once a week.

The amendment in Section 7 will enable the Department to rely more
heavily on the existing self-reporting system under BL § 75-g, which
will enable it to concentrate its resources on safety and soundness
examinations.

Sections 8, 9 and 10 are designed to bring clarity to the regulation
of a new form of electronic facility - remote deposit capture
machines, which have become prevalent since 2003, when the so-called
"Check 21" legislation was adopted to streamline and speed up the
processing of checks by encouraging the replacement of paper checks
with digital images, which have the same legal status as paper checks.

Section 13 and 14 of the bill would amend the character requirements
for mortgage bankers and mortgage brokers to make them consistent with
the similar requirements for mortgage loan originators, which were
adopted by the Legislature during the 2009 session. The Department
believes that, if the standards in Article 12-D are not conformed to
the more stringent standards set forth in Article 12-E, individuals
who are denied authority to engage in mortgage loan origination
activities will move into positions as non-MLO officers and directors
of mortgage bankers and brokers. Given the extent of the foreclosure
problem in New York, and the number of foreclosures resulting from
mortgage underwriting practices that border on the fraudulent, the
Department believes that elevating the character of officers,
directors and associated persons of mortgage bankers and brokers is
vital to protecting consumers.

Sections 15 and 16 - the amendments to BL §§ 601-a and 604-a - would
facilitate the transfer of fiduciary businesses to the branch or
agency of a foreign bank. The authority to make such transfers is
unclear under current law. This will enhance the attractiveness of the
New York license for foreign banking corporations seeking to operate
in New York.

The amendment in Section 17 of the bill would amend BL § 606(1)(e) and
is intended to provide a more accurate description of potential
capital deficiency scenarios under which the Superintendent is
authorized to take possession of an institution. Federal banking laws
now contain detailed regulatory capital requirements for banking
institutions, including target ratios that trigger mandatory closure
of insured institutions if not improved. The existing reference in BL
§ 606(1)(e) to an "impairment of capital" of a banking organization is
a narrow and outdated capital concept that alone is insufficient to
describe when the Superintendent may have adequate grounds for finding
that an institution's capital is deficient given the nature and extent
of its operations. The new language incorporates a reference to the
federal "significantly under capitalized" capital level as a
non-exclusive example of a capital level at which the Superintendent
might find an institution to have deficient capital so as to provide a
ground for possession.


Section 18 of the bill would remove references to industrial banks, a
form of banking organization that no longer exists, and make other
non-substantive changes.

Section 19 of the bill would amend General Business Law § 520-c, which
requires the Banking Department to conduct an annual survey of credit
card rates. Because credit card rates may change frequently, an annual
survey does not provide consumers with the up-to-date information they
need. The Department has been putting on its website more current
information that it obtains free of charge from other websites.
Consequently, the expenditure of the Department's funds on the current
survey seems wasteful.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

This bill is expected to generate cost efficiencies derived from more
streamlined operations.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill will take effect immediately.

summary: Permits remote deposit capture machines, clarifies the definition of capital impairment for banking institutions, modifies reporting required by banking organizations, conforms criminal provisions of the mortgage banking article to those in the mortgage loan originator article, reduces operating expenses of the banking department, and makes other technical changes.
